summary.title: SecureNova AI Platform
summary.description: SecureNova’s AI customer-support agent answers customer questions and takes actions such as order lookups and refunds. Customers log in through Auth0 (Authorization Code + PKCE, MFA). The AI agent uses an OAuth M2M client to get short-lived tokens, calls an external LLM with an API key, retrieves documents through a RAG pipeline, and executes tools through an MCP server that calls internal APIs. This model covers six identities: human users, AI agent, OAuth M2M client, LLM API key, RAG pipeline service identity and MCP server identity.

diagrams.title: AI Agent Data Flow

data.name: Customer
data.description: Human user. Auth: Auth0 login, Auth Code + PKCE, MFA. Privilege: Low (own data only).

data.name: Auth0
data.description: Third-party identity provider. Issues user tokens and M2M tokens. Privilege: Critical (controls all other identities).

data.name: LLM Provider
data.description: External LLM API. Called with a long-lived API key. Receives prompts that may contain customer data.

data.name: Chat API
data.description: Public /chat endpoint. Validates the user JWT (signature, audience, expiry, scope). Privilege: Medium.

data.name: AI Agent
data.description: Acts on behalf of the user. Holds the M2M client secret and LLM API key. Reads untrusted text. Privilege: High.

data.name: RAG Service
data.description: RAG pipeline service identity. Read-only access to the knowledge base. Privilege: Medium.

data.name: Knowledge Base
data.description: Vector store of FAQs and documents. Poisoned documents can cause indirect prompt injection.

data.name: MCP Server
data.description: MCP tool server identity. Executes tool calls (order lookup, refunds) on internal APIs. Privilege: High.

data.name: Internal API
data.description: Internal order/customer API. Accepts only scoped M2M tokens from the MCP server. Privilege: High.

threats.title: User JWT leaked in transit or logs
threats.description: The customer's access token (JWT) travels with every chat message. If it leaks from the browser, logs or an insecure network, an attacker can reuse it to chat and act as that customer.
threats.mitigation: Short token expiry; validate signature, audience, issuer and expiry on every request; HTTPS only; never put tokens in URLs or logs; MFA on login.

threats.title: Chat message or JWT modified in transit
threats.description: An attacker on an insecure network intercepts the request and changes the message content or token before it reaches the Chat API.
threats.mitigation: HTTPS/TLS only with HSTS; reject requests whose JWT signature does not verify.

threats.title: Chat endpoint flooded with requests
threats.description: An attacker sends thousands of chat requests, overloading the Chat API and burning LLM budget so real customers cannot use the service.
threats.mitigation: Rate limiting per user and IP; request size limits; WAF; spending caps on the LLM API key.

diagrams.description: End-to-end flow of one customer request: login, chat, RAG retrieval, LLM call and tool execution via MCP.
